pronunciation.approximation: Say "svarog" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Svarog".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "svarog" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Svarog" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Svarog
domains.subtitle: Sky
domains.lead: Svarog is sky, fire, smithing. The name means "Bright, clear" and belongs to the slavic tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Svarog returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in slavic myth, cult, and cultural memory.

cards.name: Unicode Restoration
cards.desc: Preserved as a flagship temple despite the unregistrable plain-ASCII form.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Svarog, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Svarog place sky, fire, smithing at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Svarog appears in slavic tradition as sky, fire, smithing. The name's meaning, "Bright, clear", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Svarog in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Svarog remains a touchstone for understanding slavic religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Ivanits, Linda J., Russian Folk Belief (1989).
Toporov, V. N., and O. N. Trubachev, Linguistic Analysis of Reconstructed Slavic Mythology.
